modularity=0.7788 across num_communities=97 signals unusually strong partition structure, and the community landmarker shows a genuine minority tail (p50=0.091 -> p99=0.75, ~8x spread) rather than saturation, so modularity-residual fit is a well-grounded primary signal. homophily=0.8617 means most nodes conform tightly to neighbor features, making homophily_violation's mismatch assumption meaningful, and its landmarker is unsaturated (mean=0.30, p50=0.26, p99=0.81) showing a real violator tail. density's landmarker shows the sharpest separation of all (p50=0.031 vs p99=0.70, ~23x), reflecting a distinct low-density minority in embedding space that offers a continuous, non-partition-based view complementary to community. attr_struct_mismatch adds a cross-modal lens (rank divergence between the graph's strong structure, modularity=0.7788, and its sparse high-dim features, feature_dim=1433 at 98.75% sparsity) with a moderate, non-saturated tail (p50=0.14 -> p99=0.69). local_affinity is deprioritized despite high homophily because its landmarker is saturated near the ceiling (mean=0.83, p50=0.84, std only 0.10, p99=1.0) with almost no separation -- consistent with an artifact of the 98.75% feature sparsity degenerating pairwise similarity, and subgraph_contrast/reconstruction/contrastive/adversarial/one_class share that same feature-reconstruction dependency so are skipped to avoid redundancy. spectral is excluded because spectral_gap=0.0 indicates a disconnected/degenerate graph, so its extreme landmarker ratio (p99/p50~216x) likely reflects trivial component-boundary artifacts rather than true anomalies. clique_density is excluded because degree heterogeneity (max_degree=168 vs avg_degree=4.08, degree_std=5.37) confounds triangle participation with hub degree, and clustering_coeff=0.2484 is only moderate, giving no direct evidence of injected dense cliques.

clique_density shows by far the sharpest landmarker tail (p50=0.0061 vs p99=0.6818, ~112x spread) against a backdrop of low overall density (0.003018) and moderate clustering (0.2484), consistent with a small population of abnormally dense/triangle-heavy subgraphs standing out from an otherwise sparse graph. community is directly supported by very high modularity (0.7788) and 97 well-separated communities plus a strongly separated score tail (p50=0.091 to p99=0.7502, ~8x), so a modularity-residual signal should cleanly flag nodes that fail to fit any community. attr_struct_mismatch has a solid tail (p50=0.1366 to p99=0.6924, ~5x) and is well-motivated by the graph's very high-dimensional, extremely sparse feature space (1433 dims, 98.75% sparsity) combined with strong homophily (0.8617): most nodes' attributes and structure agree, so cross-modal rank divergence should isolate genuine mismatches rather than sparsity noise alone. density (embedding-space LOF) also shows a strongly separated tail (p50=0.0306 to p99=0.6969, ~23x), giving a complementary global/embedding-space view distinct from the graph-native community and triangle-based clique signals. local_affinity is excluded despite high homophily because its landmarker distribution is saturated and nearly flat (p50=0.8382 to p99=1.0, ~1.2x spread), indicating the extreme feature sparsity degrades raw neighbor-affinity as a discriminative signal rather than revealing a genuine anomalous minority. spectral is excluded because although its ratio looks extreme, absolute magnitudes are near zero throughout (mean 0.0168, p99 only 0.3028) and spectral_gap=0.0 in the profile suggests the graph's spectrum lacks a well-defined gap to anchor a high-frequency anomaly signal. These four selections cover complementary mechanisms (fine-grained structural cliques, meso-scale community fit, cross-modal attribute-structure divergence, and embedding-space density) rather than redundant variants of the same signal.

The graph is extremely sparse (density=0.003, avg_degree=4.08) yet has very high modularity=0.7788 across 97 communities and moderate clustering_coeff=0.2484 -- strong mesoscale structure that a subset of nodes can violate. clique_density's landmarker shows the most extreme tail separation of any paradigm (p50=0.0061 vs p99=0.6818), indicating a small population with abnormal closure-weighted triangle participation hiding inside the overall sparsity -- exactly the structural-clique signature this metric targets. community shows a similarly strong tail (p50=0.091 vs p99=0.7502), consistent with modularity=0.7788 being high enough that most nodes fit their community tightly, leaving genuine non-conformers detectable as outliers. homophily=0.8617 is very high, meaning attribute-neighbor agreement is the dominant regime; its landmarker (p50=0.2614 vs p99=0.8087) shows a real but less extreme tail, so homophily_violation should surface the minority of nodes whose sparse (feature_sparsity=0.9875), high-dim (1433) features clash with this strong homophily pattern. attr_struct_mismatch (p50=0.1366 vs p99=0.6924) adds a complementary cross-modal check -- whether attribute-based and structure-based rankings diverge -- catching cases where structure (community/clique) and content disagree, which neither purely-structural nor purely-attribute paradigm covers alone. local_affinity was excluded despite the theoretically favorable high homophily, because its own landmarker is saturated near the top (mean=0.8268, p50=0.8382, only mild lift to p90=0.9431), i.e. it fails to separate a distinct anomalous tail on this graph and would be redundant/noisy. spectral was excluded: its landmarker is near-zero throughout (mean=0.0168, p90=0.0298) and spectral_gap=0.0 in the profile suggests a poorly-conditioned or disconnected spectrum, undermining the high-frequency-signal assumption. density (LOF/kNN in embedding space) was dropped in favor of clique_density/community since it targets a similar 'doesn't fit its neighborhood' notion but in an unspecified embedding space, making it redundant with the two topology-native structural signals already selected.

Sparse graph (density=0.003018, avg_degree=4.08) makes embedding-space density an effective orthogonal signal, with robust tail (p99=0.6969 vs p50=0.0306). Clique density captures injected collusion rings via extreme structural outliers—the score distribution has catastrophic tail separation (p99=0.6818 vs p95=0.1531), consistent with rare cliques in sparse graphs. Together these three cover structural (community), feature-space (density), and injected-substructure (clique) anomaly mechanisms. Local_affinity is excluded due to ceiling effect (p95=0.9744)—high homophily (0.8617) makes the signal mostly uniform, not right-tailed. Spectral is excluded (mean=0.0168, spectral_gap=0.0).

Community: modularity=0.4937 with 31 communities indicates strong, well-formed mesoscale structure, and the community-fit score shows real separation (p50=0.115 vs p90=0.49, p99=0.56) beyond noise. Homophily_violation: baseline homophily=0.659 is high enough that feature-neighbor mismatches are meaningful, and the score distribution shows a clean, non-saturated tail (p50=0.25 -> p90=0.78 -> p95=0.99 -> p99=1.0), the sharpest genuine separation among all landmarkers. Density: degree_std=30.81 with max_degree=789 (power-law) and clustering_coeff=0.32 produce genuine embedding-space sparsity; the density score is tightly concentrated near zero for most nodes but jumps 64x from p50 (0.0025) to p99 (0.1603), a classic small, sharply separated outlier tail. These three cover complementary views (attribute-neighbor mismatch, global community adherence, embedding density) with minimal overlap.
